clue.text: Old man used to land fish

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a boss, foreman or elderly fellow
read literally, one who wields a gaff, the hooked pole anglers use to haul a catch aboard

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: a gaff lands fish, so the man using it is jokily named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a foreman or elderly man is called this, and the word also suggests someone who gaffs fish.

clue.text: In a frenzy, though apparently claiming to be all right

parts.note: saying 'I am' is claiming to be something
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone in a frenzy keeps insisting they are perfectly fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though apparently' joins the pieces; split, the word reads as someone saying 'I am fine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Running wild in a frenzy is to run this way, a borrowing from Malay.

clue.text: Another setback as the result of stiff breeze?

definitions.meaning: a further blow or misfortune, newly arrived
literally a new gust of wind blowing

explanation.definitionFit: A fresh blow is a new misfortune, and literally a new gust of wind in a stiff breeze.

clue.text: The old familiar story traveller has to dine on

parts.note: a rep is a commercial traveller, a travelling salesperson
to eat is to dine on food

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman tells the same tired tale over dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun or retold tale is a familiar story heard once more.

clue.text: Main part of evidence showing that Federal agents are holding right girl

indicators.note: the agents hold the next pieces inside them

parts.note: G-men are FBI agents, government men
Ava is a girl's name

explanation.surface: FBI agents detaining the right young woman provide the heart of the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal term for the essential, most serious part of a complaint or charge.

clue.text: Sign of impending storm in crowd (150 university players)

parts.note: a gathering is a crowd of people
CL is 150 in Roman numerals
OUDS is the Oxford University Dramatic Society, a student acting club

explanation.surface: A big audience assembles to watch a university drama troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; the two words of 'university players' together give one abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkening skies massing overhead are a warning that a storm is coming.

clue.text: Animal seen to run on Mount Etna

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another follows beneath it
to mount is to set up or stage, so the letters of the volcano's name are set out afresh

parts.note: to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A creature is spotted running across the slopes of a Sicilian volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' rearranges ETNA into ANTE; 'on' puts LOPE beneath it. 'Mount Etna' reads as a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift horned grazing beast of Africa and Asia is one example of an animal.

clue.text: Bitter and sour over some macabre calamity

indicators.note: in a down clue, over signals the letters are turned upwards
some of the phrase is taken, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A sharp, sour remark is made about some grisly disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes BRECA from inside 'macabre calamity'; 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare adjective meaning harsh-tasting, tart and sharp in flavour or temper.

clue.text: Simple working editors having no right to proceed cautiously

parts.note: easy means simple

indicators.note: the remaining letters are worked into a new order
editors having no right means the editors lose that letter, so it is struck out of the word

explanation.surface: Editors who have lost their right-hand man are told to go gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' removes R from EDITORS, leaving EDITOS; 'working' rearranges it as DOES IT. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said to urge someone to go slowly and carefully.

clue.text: It's attractive to phoney characters

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are treated as loose characters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something proves alluring to people who are fakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' means letters here: the letters of 'to phoney' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irresistibly alluring, drawing people as a jar of nectar draws bees.

clue.text: Article taking one a little way to becoming a believer in God

parts.note: the is the definite article
I is the Roman numeral one
ST, short for street, is a way in abbreviated form

explanation.surface: A writer's piece takes someone a short distance towards faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' and 'to becoming' are links; 'a little way' means an abbreviated way, ST for street.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds that a deity exists is a believer in God.

clue.text: Star possessing great physical attraction?

definitions.meaning: a sun or other object in the sky
jokily, a gorgeous figure, a divine physique

explanation.definitionFit: A planet or star in the sky, and playfully someone with a divinely attractive figure.

clue.text: Outstanding impression make by drunken replacement

parts.note: high means intoxicated
a relief is a person replacing another on duty

explanation.surface: A tipsy stand-in makes a striking impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A carving whose figures stand far out from the background is a sculpted impression that stands out.

clue.text: Where trouble's expected to end in a fight

definitions.meaning: from the northern English saying 'there's trouble at t'mill', the factory floor
an old slang word for a boxing bout or brawl

explanation.walkthrough: 'to end in' is a link. The saying is a famous Yorkshire catchphrase about strife at the factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory is where the saying places trouble, and in old slang the word is a fistfight.

clue.text: Businessman who takes a drink on the way back

indicators.note: back signals the letters of the road are read in reverse

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI in crosswords
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A merchant stops for a pint on the motorway home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who takes a' and 'on the' are links. The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, and crosswords write its number as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who brings goods in from abroad is a kind of businessman.

clue.text: Going back to the lapel lining's number one fashion

indicators.note: the lapel and fashion line, or surround, the next piece

parts.note: revers is a turned-back lapel on a coat
on means in fashion
I is the Roman numeral one, and also the first person

explanation.surface: A return to old styles makes the jacket's lapel lining fashionable again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A return to a former state or owner is a going back.

clue.text: Stick to drill, though wearisome to fellow members

parts.note: a club is a heavy stick
to bore is to drill a hole

explanation.surface: Someone sticks to their DIY drilling, though it tires their friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'though' are links; the definition describes the tiresome person rather than naming them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious person at a social club, tiresome to the other members.

clue.text: Call to rise as girls in the chorus do

definitions.meaning: a shout to get someone out of bed

definitions.text: as girls in the chorus do
definitions.meaning: chorus line dancers literally display their legs

explanation.definitionFit: A naval wake-up cry to get out of bed, and literally what high-kicking dancers do.

clue.text: It's useless to instal one in the vehicle

indicators.note: to instal something in a place is to put it inside

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Trying to fit someone inside the van is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's', 'to' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort in vain is futile, ineffectual, achieving nothing.

clue.text: Stoppage to assist reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A halt is called to help reform proceed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of standstill or equilibrium, with no flow or movement.

clue.text: Carriage for one on patrol

definitions.meaning: someone who walks round an area inspecting it

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. The second sense is the literal walker-around.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name of a pram, and also a person who walks round a district.

clue.text: Defence gets one bail improperly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: In court, a defendant secures bail by dubious means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim of being elsewhere at the time is a defence against a charge.

clue.text: Girl, we're told, with characteristic responsibility

indicators.note: what we are told is heard spoken

parts.note: Jean is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is reported to be reliably responsible.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a unit of heredity responsible for a characteristic.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of DNA governs an inherited trait, so it bears responsibility for a characteristic.

clue.text: Urge order in oil rig

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
to rig is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a bid is a command or order

explanation.surface: An order comes through on an offshore oil platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil rig' poses as a drilling platform, but 'rig' is the anagram signal working on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual desire or drive is a strong urge.

clue.text: Not fit to appear in deshabille?

definitions.meaning: partly dressed, literally without a suit on

explanation.walkthrough: 'to appear' is a link. Deshabille means a state of undress.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-matched or inappropriate, and playfully having no suit on.

clue.text: Non-skaters who are in command?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., people off the ice

explanation.definitionFit: Commissioned commanders in the forces, and jokily people off the ice.

clue.text: Model in synthetic resin from deposit in hot springs

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
synthetic means artificially made, so the letters are remade

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A model made from man-made resin is found near hot springs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'synthetic' rearranges RESIN into SINER and 'in' puts T inside it. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A crust of silica or lime left by mineral springs is this kind of deposit.
